item.title: Trump says he does not know if Iran is going to 'give up yet'
item.description:
By Steve Holland and Kanishka Singh

WASHINGTON, Sept 29 (Reuters) - President Donald Trump said on Tuesday he does not know if Iran is going to "give up yet" but cast the country as doing "very poorly" in its war with the US.

DETAILS AND QUOTES:

• "I don't know if they are going to give up yet but they'll give up," Trump told reporters.

• "They are doing very poorly," he added.

• A US blockade has cut Iran's financial lifeline - oil exports, and economic costs of the war have made life tougher for Iranians.

item.title: Morocco's king appoints first woman prime minister following election
item.description:
By Ahmed Eljechtimi

RABAT, Sept 29 (Reuters) - King Mohammed VI appointed Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri on Tuesday as Morocco's first woman prime minister after her liberal-centrist party came out on top in a September 23 parliamentary election, the royal palace said.

The king asked El Mansouri to form a new government, the palace said in a statement.

item.title: UAE vice president visits Saudi Arabia in first visit since rift
item.description:
Sept 29 (Reuters) - UAE Vice President Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed Al Nahyan visited Saudi Arabia on Tuesday and met with the Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman and the kingdom's defence minister, the first visit by a senior UAE official to the kingdom since a deep rift emerged between the two Gulf powers last year.

The visit, following an invitation by Saudi Defence Minister Prince Khalid bin Salman, occurred as Riyadh faces increasing pressure from the Iran-backed Houthis, who have for weeks fired salvos of missiles and drones at the kingdom.

item.title: Who are the Emiratis behind crisis-hit Manchester City?
item.description:
Over the course of nearly two decades, Emirati money has turned once mediocre Manchester City into one of the most dominant teams in world football. 

Now, the club face substantial sanctions and potentially even automatic relegation from the Premier League.

In February 2023, the league brought 115 charges against City for breaching financial rules and failing to cooperate with its investigations.

item.title: As Iran’s grip on Hormuz weakens, what leverage does Tehran have left?
item.description: Six months into the war, Iran's grip on the Strait of Hormuz is weakening. The world is slowly learning to live with it, oil flows are recovering, alternative routes are expanding and Tehran's own economy is bearing the cost of keeping the waterway under pressure.

item.title: US imposes sanctions on 13 tied to Iran weapons procurement
item.description:
By Andrea Shalal

WASHINGTON, Sept 29 - The US government announced fresh sanctions on Tuesday against 13 individuals and entities, including some based in Russia, China, Hong Kong and Pakistan, saying they helped Iran procure weapons and components.

The sanctions announced by the Treasury and State departments are part of the Trump administration's effort to isolate Iran economically and force it to negotiate an end to the war that began with a US-Israeli strike on Iran on February 28.

item.description: The latest sanctions come after the two sides held another round of indirect talks over a possible deal to end the war.
